### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/README.md`, `packages/spec/liveness/action.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/tools.mdx`  _(via escalate_case (literal, a string literal in fixture), support_case (literal, a string literal in fixture))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/README.md`, `packages/spec/liveness/action.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2f122b6e47dd01264d1a3c4d2fc7946fc31f3f2e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8cb48e7e154d3b346abb2c6af1acb8cd8191992d` — the merge of head `7faf0e9f63c7a37478b86af29f713f5697ea1970` into base `2f122b6e47dd01264d1a3c4d2fc7946fc31f3f2e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8cb48e7e154d3b346abb2c6af1acb8cd8191992d && git checkout 8cb48e7e154d3b346abb2c6af1acb8cd8191992d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2f122b6e47dd01264d1a3c4d2fc7946fc31f3f2e 7faf0e9f63c7a37478b86af29f713f5697ea1970 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2f122b6e47dd01264d1a3c4d2fc7946fc31f3f2e && git merge --no-ff 7faf0e9f63c7a37478b86af29f713f5697ea1970

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2f122b6e47dd01264d1a3c4d2fc7946fc31f3f2e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2f122b6e47dd01264d1a3c4d2fc7946fc31f3f2e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7faf0e9f63c7a37478b86af29f713f5697ea1970`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #20323 (body and all five comments — triage 5860351140, claims 5861374979 / 5863199486, release 5862791758, dev report 5864933100); PR #20398 (body, 19-file list, net diff against `main` at merge-base `15bf186f`); the 35 check-runs on the head (33 success; 2 skipped by design — Console Pin Gate, whose path filter is `.objectui-sha` plus the console scripts, none touched; Packed-tarball smoke, opt-in). Verification was read-only: `git fetch` / `git show` / `git grep` against refs in this checkout and against the objectui pin `f8a9d0fb05` in the sibling checkout; nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set
- `ActionSchema.aria` narrows from `AriaPropsSchema.optional()` to `retiredKey(...)`, a `never` slot: any authored value is refused at parse with the prescription, and the input type is `never` for `tsc`. Both authored coordinates (`actions[]`, `objects[].actions[]`) refuse through the same slot; pinned in `action.test.ts` and `aria-carrier-tombstones.test.ts` (object-nested case included). RIGHT. Premise re-verified at the objectui pin: 0 readers of an action's `aria` on any action surface (`action:button/icon/menu/group/bar`, the row and bulk menus, the quick-actions bar); the only `schema.aria` readers are placing nodes (`record:*` components, `ListView`); icon-only renderers name from `schema.label` (`action-icon.tsx:243`, `action-menu.tsx:341`), so triage's reversal condition does not hold. Direction is RETIRE per the triage record; no maintainer word reversed it.
- Refusal shape: `invalid_type` at path `aria`, no root `unrecognized_keys`, message head pinned. RIGHT — that is the tombstone's own issue, and the anti-vacuity is real: a bare delete on this `strictObject` would answer `unrecognized_keys` without the prescription.
- Tombstone on a `strictObject` rather than the guidance-map route. RIGHT — `retired-key.ts`'s own docblock names closed shapes as a supported case (the prescription is the payload), the same schema already carries `execute` as a `retiredKey` tombstone, and the ledger discipline follows the tombstone route consistently (row kept and regraded; authorable-surface row marked `[RETIRED]`, not deleted).
- `AriaPropsSchema` untouched and still live on `page.aria`, `page.components[].aria`, the list view `aria` and element props; control pinned. RIGHT — a key retirement, not a def retirement.

ADR-0087
- D2 `action-aria-removed`: `toMajor: 18`, `retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `stripKeys` via `mapCollection` over `actions[]` and `objects[].actions[]`, one notice per stripped key, fixture with `expectedNotices: 2`, copy-on-write control and idempotence pinned. Replay sites: authored sources are NOT replayed (the loader skips retired entries; the tombstone refuses and the house sentence sends the author to `os migrate meta --from 17`, which replays the chain) — RIGHT; stored seams — `applyConversionsToStoredItem` pins `includeRetired: true` and wraps `action` / `object` rows into `actions` / `objects`, so both at-rest coordinates are reached, pinned by two tests — RIGHT; artifact door — `applyArtifactForwardConversions` replays with `includeRetired: true` over the whole stack shape, where actions live only at those two paths — RIGHT. The third `ActionSchema` embedding (`MetadataTypeRegistryEntry.actions`, plugin code, and its `MetadataTypeInfoResponse` projection) is neither a stack source nor a stored row; no walker reaches it and the tombstone (`tsc` plus parse) covers it; the conversion docblock states this boundary. RIGHT.
- D3 `action-aria-retired` as its own family (ruling B on #17152), non-empty `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria`; step 18 `conversionIds` and `rationale` extended; `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR[18]` gains `ui/Action:aria`, matching the authorable-surface spelling. Registered under protocol 18 while shipping on 17.5.0 is the chart sibling's convention and ADR-0087's amended two-axis rule. RIGHT. The generated `migrations/registry.ts` matches its entry files (Lint & Repo Gates carries that step; success).
- D4 artifacts (`spec-changes.json`, upgrade guide) unchanged. RIGHT — both project protocol 16 to 17 only; every other 18-registered conversion (chart-config-aria, permission-rls-tags, currency-config-precision) is equally absent; `check:spec-changes` / `check:upgrade-guide` ran green.
- Changeset marker: the adr-0087 `registered` marker names `action-aria-removed` and `action-aria-retired`; both ids resolve at the head (Check Changeset runs `check-adr-0087-registration` against the merge-base; success).

Ledger and baselines
- `liveness/action.json` `aria`: `live` to `dead`, `verifiedAt` 2026-09-28, note in the house REMOVED template and recording the uncited PARTIAL claim. The row carried only `status` and `note` before (no `authorWarn`), so no advisory-lint non-warn pin is owed. RIGHT. `state-counts.md` (action live 46 to 45, dead 3 to 4; totals 939 / 163) is arithmetically consistent; the `action/aria` undrilled-container row goes (a `never` slot has nothing to drill); the README action row now says the dead set is four. Spec property liveness check-run: success.
- `authorable-surface/ui.json`: `ui/Action:aria [RETIRED]`. `api-surface` and `json-schema.manifest` unchanged — correct for a key tombstone (both record def and export existence, not key sets).

Public surface and docs
- No exported symbol removed; the `Action` input type's `aria` becomes `undefined`-only. objectui at the pin: `ActionRunner.ts:410` mirrors `SpecActionInput['aria']`, which resolves to `undefined` and compiles; `actionKeys.ts` lists `aria` in the spec-owned key set, and the tombstone keeps the key in the shape. Console Pin Gate was skipped by its path filter, so the sibling compile is dev-probed rather than gate-measured; nothing the pinned sibling imports is removed by this diff. RIGHT.
- Served schema: `stripUnauthorableProperties` drops `{ not: {} }` property nodes structurally (`acceptsNothing`), so Studio's derived "More fields" stops offering `aria` once the release is pinned. RIGHT.
- Docs: `actions.mdx` interface block loses `aria?: AriaProps` with corrective prose; `widget-contract.mdx` carrier sentence corrected; three reference tables regenerated (the nested `Action.aria` table gone). No remaining page teaches `aria` on an action (grep at head). RIGHT.
- First-party authors of an action `aria`: 0 in this repository at the head (`aria:` over `examples/**`, `skills/**`, `packages/**`, `apps/**` outside spec src, tests and generated files hits only i18n locale bundles, the page and view form translations, and CHANGELOGs); the four Type Check check-runs are green, so no TS author survives the `never` type; objectui at the pin authors `aria` only on its own live carriers (record components, list views, chart configs), and its one action-shaped type test expects `{ aria: 'label' }` refused, which still holds. HotCRM `2f7b2326` 0-on-actions is dev-measured with a control (out of repo; not re-measured here).

Residual, advisory (no accept-set or surface effect): two published `src/**/*.zod.ts` comments now name the action as a live `AriaProps` carrier — `i18n.zod.ts:8-11` (a dated measurement note that already lists `ChartConfigSchema`, retired by #17751 and left uncorrected there, so this PR is at parity with the precedent) and `dashboard.zod.ts:1129` (the parenthetical saying `action.aria` carries the shape and the ledger grades it PARTIAL). Carry as a one-line follow-up beside the objectui sub-issue.

### ② Semver level

- `'@objectstack/spec': minor` with the BREAKING banner, the FROM to TO table, the one-line fix, the house `os migrate meta --from 17` sentence and the ADR-0087 `registered` marker. RIGHT: ADR-0087 (amended 2026-09-13, #18003) ships a pre-GA metadata-facing retirement as `minor` with the banner and its disposition entry; `check-changeset-no-major` (Check Changeset, success) refuses `major` in the launch window. Only `@objectstack/spec` publishes from this diff (`src/**/*.zod.ts`, `liveness/`, `dist`; `content/docs` is the docs site, not a package), so a single bump is correct. The tombstone's `17.5.0` is the next minor on the 17.4.0 line and matches the sibling spelling.
- Clause-②: yes — declared identically in the PR body, the changeset and both claims. The arm is omitted, which the rule permits (at most one arm), and the BREAKING banner carries the breaking signal the registration gate reads. It is an accept-set narrowing, correctly declared, tombstoned and registered.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations (seven), each answered:
1. Worktree created from the branch (dispatch-ordered RESUME), no empty-branch push — process; the six hand-over commits were re-read and corrected in `68b038ef`; the net diff is what is judged. Answered.
2. Two `main` merges through `os-regen-merge.sh` with deferred regenerations — the net three-dot diff is clean (19 files; the conversion, the D3 entry and the retired key each appear exactly once in their registries); the head's check-runs are green. Answered.
3. `liveness/README.md`, one sentence outside the claim's surface — RIGHT to take: `liveness` is in `@objectstack/spec` `files[]`, the row said the dead set was three, which this change made false, and the retirement playbook's ledger step names the README row; the PR body names the fix with evidence, as the os-dev in-place rule requires. The rule's second obligation — amending the claim's declared file surface in the same round — is not on the card (no amended claim comment). Escalated to the seat as an owed one-line claim amendment; not a diff defect.
4. Consumer suites and spec typecheck measured at `8dd3a2ce`, not the head — superseded by the check-runs on `7faf0e9f` (Test Core 6/6, Type Check x4, Build Core, Dogfood, Temporal). Answered.
5. One locked run cut by a timeout and a stray vitest child killed by PID — process hygiene with no diff content; the re-run was under the lock, and the head's check-runs are the verdict. Answered.
6. Commit trailers follow AGENTS.md's model-free pair — verified on all eleven authored commits; the hand-over merge `8cbcfa46` carries no trailer (a merge commit; the pre-push hook accepted the push). Answered.
7. Refusal pin asserts the Zod issue kind and message head rather than an ADR-0112 `code` plus `status` — RIGHT: ADR-0112 governs the API error envelope; a `retiredKey()` refusal is a Zod parse issue with no HTTP status, as the family docblock (`aria-carrier-tombstones.test.ts:36-38`) records; the `invalid_type`-at-`aria`-with-no-root-`unrecognized_keys` assertion is the correct anti-vacuity shape. Answered.

`open_questions`: none declared; none found.

Out-of-scope findings (two), correctly carried and not folded: objectui `ActionDefaultInspector` `RETIRED_FIELDS` plus the `ActionRunner` mirror (the seat's sub-issue after landing, per triage note 3); #19332's waiting item receives the disposition (the seat's write after landing). Add the advisory residual above to the same follow-up.

Console Pin Gate skipped (path filter) and Packed-tarball smoke skipped (opt-in) are by design, not gaps in this head's verdict.
